rationale:
The requirement obliges the review prompt to give a report template with four sections. These are the revised text of every group requirement (including new split ones) as complete paste-ready directives, the revised text of affected requirements outside the group, the mechanical changes (new full names and added examples), and the design questions.

`tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[the_review_prompt_gives_a_report_template]` is marked {test}. It takes the `## Report` section of the raw review prompt from `review_prompt()`. The `section` helper bounds that section at the next heading of the same or a higher level, outside code fences, so the `###` subsections stay inside it. It then calls `assert_text_in_order`, which panics if any phrase is missing or out of order.

The phrases map to the four obligations:
- `### Revised text` and "as complete directives ready to paste, including new split requirements" cover the first section.
- `### Edits outside the group` and "revised text of other requirements your changes make stale" cover the second.
- `### Mechanical changes` and "list new full names and added examples" cover the third.
- `### Design questions` covers the fourth.

The assertions are real, because a missing or reordered section or description fails the test. A prompt that dropped a section or its content would be caught. The requirement fixes no section order, so the order check is a stricter assertion but not a wrong one.

The requirement has no other modes or boundaries. I found no gap.

text: The review prompt MUST give a report template with these sections:
- the revised text of every requirement in the group, including new split requirements, as complete directives ready to paste;
- the revised text of requirements outside the group that the changes affect;
- the mechanical changes, including new full names and added examples;
